messages:
alexj: Heads-up: noticed a small spike in routed fallbacks to the degen path yesterday. Root cause looks like fncall responses missing the top-level "items" field intermittently. Anyone else seeing this?
maria_t: Yep. Saw traces. It's ~0.03% of requests but accounts for a lot of billing churn because fallbacks route to the expensive path.
priya: Do we have telemetry that distinguishes schema/contract violations from tool runtime errors? Dashboard currently lumps them together.
devops-bot: deploy: rolled back validate-v2 on canary at 09:12 UTC due to adapter 502s.
lee_oncall: I dug traces — adapter returned 200 with { 'status':'ok' } but missing the "items" array. Our validator treats that as a soft-fail and we trigger fallback. Problem: routing policy treats any fallback as a full-cost route. Proposing a soft-fallback route that uses cheaper model variants.
alexj: We need to surface contract violations in Console per-route. Right now the info is only in raw logs. Proposal: add a "contract_violation_rate" metric and surface the top offending prompt templates.
maria_t: Agree. Also change sampling: if violation rate spikes, sample 100% for 10m, not the 1% default. We currently miss context.
priya: Is it straightforward to add a "contract_quality_score" to telemetry? Could be ratio(validated_calls / total_calls) per route/model.
lee_oncall: Score is easy, but watch out for intentional partial responses — sometimes "items" can be null by design. Need a per-route flag like "nullableItemsAllowed" to avoid false positives.
alexj: Example schema we saw: ```json
{
  "type":"object",
  "properties":{
    "items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}},
    "metadata":{"type":"object"}
  },
  "required":["items"]
}
``` We should support per-route overrides to relax "required" during canary windows.
maria_t: UX idea: Console shows a one-click "soften contract" toggle for canary that: 1) marks policy permissive, 2) routes to permissive pool with lower-cost profile, 3) bumps failure sampling. Guarded by RBAC.
priya: Billing worry — if permissive pool still costs the same, teams will be surprised. Need clear labeling.
lee_oncall: Implementation idea: permissive pool maps to quantized variant (q4) and lower-priority instances so unit cost is lower. Console should display expected unit cost delta when enabling.
alexj: For telemetry, add a "validator_reason" tag (e.g., missing_field, type_mismatch, parse_error) so alerting rules can target real contract regressions.
maria_t: Also we should escalate if contract_violation_rate > 0.01% for 30m. That should flip sampling to continuous until resolved.
priya: For rollout semantics: will teams be able to schedule permissive windows (e.g., 02:00-06:00) or enable manually? Nighttime windows reduce user impact.
alexj: Expose schedule in API + Console, and allow reversible API flag for automation.
lee_oncall: Action items: (1) add contract_violation_rate metric + validator_reason tag, (2) implement permissive route mapping to cheaper model variant, (3) console toggle + schedule UI, (4) bump failure sampling to 100% for 10m after alert then decay. I'll take (1) and (2). @maria_t can you own (3)?
maria_t: I'll own the console toggle. Mock UI by EOD and I'll loop in design and product for wording. Need a backend flag too.
devops-bot: incident: created ticket INF-4321 for routing-permissive-workflow. Assigned: lee_oncall.
priya: :thumbsup: thanks — please add a short doc describing billing implications and recommended default schedules.
alexj: Adding that doc to the ticket now. Closing loop: let's try a 48-hour canary once we have metrics and UI.
